newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TRANSVAAL CHANGE MIND ON NEW NAME.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TRANSVAAL CHANGE MIND ON NEW NAME.

text.p: The 108-year-old Transvaal Rugby Union (TRU) has bowed to political pressure by changing its name to the Gauteng Lions Rugby Union.
The TRU reversed their earlier intention to become the Golden Lions Rugby Union at their annual meeting in Johannesburg on Monday night.

The announcement of the name change had caused a storm of debate. The old administrative region of Transvaal was reborn as Gauteng -- meaning place of gold -- two years ago but the TRU said they saw no reason to include it in their name.
After the annual meeting TRU president Louis Luyt admitted: "We don't want to revisit this problem in a year's time. We will be under political pressure if we don't incorporate Gauteng in our name."
The four other unions carrying the name Transvaal in their title are also undergoing change.

South Eastern Transvaal have already become Mpumalanga; Northern Transvaal are expected to become the Blue Bulls; Eastern Transvaal have launched a competition to find a new name; and Northern Transvaal are planning to become North West.
The Gauteng Lions will play under their new name for the first time when they host the Wellington Hurricanes of New Zealand on Saturday.
